snow: WordNet sense-1 gloss ('precipitation falling from clouds in the form of ice crystals') does NOT say white; 'white' appears only in sense 2 ('a layer of snowflakes (white crystals of frozen water)...'). Reported as a coverage fact; the rule is not padded to force white onto snow.

sun & lamp/light: their glosses say 'source of light' / 'source of (visible) illumination'; bare 'light' is excluded and the noun 'illumination' is not in the bright pole set, so these prototypical illumination referents get NO bright hit under the strict rule. Recorded, not padded.

coal: noun sense-1 (fossil fuel) names no color despite coal being prototypically black; the only illumination token is 'glowing' (bright) in sense 2 (a hot ember) -- so the definition's illumination polarity for coal is BRIGHT, opposite the dark prototype.
